title: Adaptive client prefetch + idempotent resumable streams: multi-language SDK requirements
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Product requirements for introducing an adaptive prefetching layer plus idempotent resumable streaming primitives in our Python/TS/Go SDKs. Objective: reduce tail latency and token cost for typical conversational and embedding workloads while preserving strong compatibility and safe retries across client versions.
problem_statement: Applications using long-running streams (chat, audio transcriptions, long embedding lists) experience two main issues: (1) regressions from naive prefetching that break backward-compatible SDK behavior and server quotas, and (2) brittle retry semantics for partially-consumed streams leading to duplicate results or data loss when connections drop. Current SDK APIs expose streaming as a firehose or simple iterator with no built-in idempotency, and client teams build bespoke solutions leading to inconsistent behavior across languages.
goals: Define a cross-language SDK primitive for resumable streams with stable resume cursors and idempotency tokens
Add optional adaptive prefetch policies (size/time-based) that are safe under quota and cost constraints
Ensure backwards compatibility: new features must not break existing streaming or pagination contracts
Provide clear acceptance criteria, telemetry, migration path, and rollout strategy for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs
non_goals: Server-side protocol changes beyond support for resume cursors and idempotency tokens
Rewriting existing customer SDK apps to use new primitives during initial rollout
Implementing model-level batching optimizations (server handles batching)
functional_requirements: SDKs must expose a ResumableStream abstraction with .resume(cursor) and .snapshot() methods
Resume cursors must be opaque strings generated by the server; SDK must persist and present them unmodified
Each streamed session must accept an optional idempotency token header generated client-side; SDK should offer a secure default generator and allow custom tokens
Adaptive prefetch policy configurable per-call: parameters (max_lookahead_tokens, max_messages, max_bytes, time_window_ms)
Prefetch must be rate-aware: SDK should respect server-provided rate/quota headers and gracefully backoff prefetching
When a connection drop occurs, SDK must attempt resume using the last snapshot and idempotency token within 120s by default
SDKs must provide a safe fallback: if resume fails, deliver a deterministic error that includes ‘resume_not_supported’ code and the last-snapshot metadata
Provide a streaming-to-pagination adapter: convert a ResumableStream into a PaginatedIterator and vice-versa for client convenience
All APIs must support both sync and async calling patterns for languages that support them (Python/TS/Go)
api_surface: Python: ResumableStream(client, model, *, prefetch_policy=None, idempotency_token=None) -> async iterator with snapshot() and resume(cursor) methods
TypeScript: createResumableStream(options) -> AsyncIterable with getCursor(), resume(cursor) and setPrefetchPolicy(policy)
Go: type ResumableStream interface { Next(ctx) (Chunk, error); Snapshot() string; Resume(ctx, cursor) error; ConfigurePrefetch(Policy) }
PrefetchPolicy structure (cross-language): {mode: 'off'|'conservative'|'aggressive', max_lookahead_tokens: int, max_messages: int, max_bytes: int, jitter_ms: int}
Telemetry hooks: onPrefetchStart, onPrefetchHit, onPrefetchThrottle, onResumeAttempt, onResumeSuccess, onResumeFailure
compatibility_constraints: Server must continue to support existing streaming APIs; new resume cursors are additive and optional
New SDK default behavior must be backward compatible: prefetch disabled by default for major-minor conservative rollout
Client-side idempotency token format must not collide with existing tokens; SDK should namespace tokens with 'rw-id:' prefix
Prefetch behavior must be togglable via environment variable and per-call option to support platform customers on Dedicated/Private deployments
Behavior when interacting with older server versions (no resume support): SDK must surface a clear recoverable error and fall back to non-resumable streaming
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): release experimental prefetch and resumable stream in Python SDK behind feature flag; monitor telemetry for duplicates and latency
Phase 2 (polyglot beta): release TS and Go SDKs with feature flag; collect cross-language parity issues
Phase 3 (opt-in GA): enable for new SDK installs with prefetch off by default; document migration guidance
Phase 4 (on by default): after telemetry shows <=1% duplicate events and no customer regressions, flip safe conservative prefetch on by default in minor release
Rollback: ability to disable feature globally via service-side kill switch and per-client env var
migration_strategy: Provide adapter shims that map existing streaming iterators to ResumableStream with no code change; publish migration guide with examples for Python/TS/Go. For customers on Dedicated/Private, ship server-side compatibility flags and a local toggle. Offer a temporary compatibility shim release (minor version) that exposes resume APIs but keeps default runtime identical.
acceptance_criteria: SDK unit and integration tests covering resume success/failure and idempotency across network flakiness
End-to-end test against staging serving layer with simulated connection drops demonstrates resume success >= 98% within 120s for supported endpoints
Prefetch telemetry shows no more than 5% increase in token usage for conservative mode compared to baseline, and tail 95th p99 latency improves by at least 10% for chat workloads
Backward compatibility test suite passes against two previous server protocol versions
Documentation and migration guide published and linked in SDK release notes
Security review completed for idempotency token defaults and any local persistence of cursors
qa_tests: Simulate flaky networks: drop TCP after N messages and verify resume semantics and idempotency behavior
Quota simulation: inject quota-exceeded headers and assert SDK throttles prefetch and surfaces prefetch_quota_exceeded event
Cross-language parity: run the same streaming workload in Python/TS/Go and assert identical sequence of chunks and cursor values
Backward server compatibility: point SDKs at older server that lacks resume and assert graceful fallback error and no crash
Stress test aggressive prefetch mode to quantify token blow-up and ensure safety limits enforced
